items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Don recorded 4 numbers with a band that included ... myself on trumpet ... Lois Deppe and Don, vocals.

ctx.x: There was a big surprise waiting for us on opening night. Fess Williams band had left and so had Arthur Gibbs. The second band was Horace Henderson. Fletcher had to aid his younger brother by hiring Benny Carter who had left Charlie Johnson and Rex Stewart especially for Horace's debut at the Savoy.

We were on the stand that had been occupied by Fess Williams. I sat on the end on the right side of the stand, Frank Newton on my left and Dickie Wells left of Frank. Cecil stood in the middle, Lester Carr left of Cecil, Harold McFerran in the back, Mack Walker and Lloyd were on the same level as Don.

Rex Stewart was on the left side of the other bandstand and that put him and I next to each other. From the very first night until Horace finished at the end of February it was a battle of jazz which ended in a draw. Benny and Rex did a lot for Horace's orchestra. Benny played much more than I had heard him play with Charlie Johnson orchestra and Rex was the fastest man I had ever heard on trumpet. He was better than he was when I first saw him with Fletcher in Cincinnati and I especially liked his fast execution…
